ch09.d.kind: What happens after the impact: bounce apart, bounce less, stick together, or be pushed apart by a spring
ch09.d.kind2: What happens after the impact: bounce apart, bounce less, or stick together
ch09.d.m2p: Mass of puck 2, initially at rest (puck 1 is 1 kg)
ch09.d.v1: Initial velocity of cart 1; to the right is positive
ch09.d.v1p: Initial velocity of puck 1, to the right
ch09.d.v2: Initial velocity of cart 2; negative means it comes towards cart 1
ch09.d.e: Relative speed of separation after the impact ÷ relative speed of approach before it
ch09.d.E: Kinetic energy the released spring gives to the two carts
ch09.d.arrows: $p_1$, $p_2$ above the carts and $p_\text{tot}$ above the centre of mass
ch09.d.b: Distance between the line of motion of puck 1 and the centre of puck 2; 0 is head-on, at most 0.29 m (the pucks always collide, whatever the mass)
ch09.t.goal.p: With no external force the total momentum $p_1 + p_2$ is the same before and after the collision
ch09.t.goal.K: Kinetic energy is conserved only in an elastic collision: momentum conservation and energy conservation are separate statements
ch09.t.obs.ptot: $p$ graph: $p_1$ and $p_2$ jump at the impact, their sum $p_\text{tot}$ stays flat
ch09.t.obs.elastic: Elastic, equal masses (default): the carts swap velocities and $K_\text{tot}$ is unchanged
ch09.t.obs.stick: Perfectly inelastic: the carts stick and move together at $v_\text{cm}$; the largest loss of $K_\text{tot}$
ch09.t.obs.explode: Explosion: carts at rest fly apart in opposite directions, $p_\text{tot} = 0$ throughout while $K_\text{tot}$ rises
ch09.t.obs.cm: Centre of mass (⊕): moves at constant velocity before and after the collision; $x_\text{cm}(t)$ is a straight line
ch09.t.assume: Frictionless level track; the collision is instantaneous; cart size drawn according to mass. In the graphs the cart 1 curve has a pale band, so it stays visible under another curve (e.g. $K_1 = K_2$ in an equal-mass explosion)
ch09.k.goal.vec: Momentum is a vector: $\vec p_1 + \vec p_2$ is the same before and after the collision
ch09.k.goal.comp: The $x$ and $y$ components are conserved separately
ch09.k.obs.diagram: Momentum sum: $\vec p_1$ and $\vec p_2$ added tail to head reach the same $\vec p_\text{tot}$ after the collision
ch09.k.obs.right: Equal masses, elastic (default): after the collision the pucks move off at 90° to each other
ch09.k.obs.headon: $b = 0$: a head-on collision, the same as the 1D case
ch09.k.obs.stick: Perfectly inelastic: the pucks stick and move on at the centre-of-mass velocity
ch09.k.assume: Frictionless table; smooth pucks (the impulse acts along the line of centres); puck rotation ignored; puck size drawn according to mass. In the graphs the puck 1 curve has a pale band, so it stays visible under another curve
